name: ISWIM
note: Landin; paper language ancestor of ML
typeSystem: A paper design with no fixed concrete syntax or built-in type system: Peter Landin proposed ISWIM ('If you See What I Mean') as an abstract framework, built on the lambda calculus plus imperative extensions, that any number of concrete surface languages could be instances of.
runtime: ISWIM was never implemented as a language of its own; its operational account used Landin's abstract-machine framework. ISWIM's language ideas, rather than a documented direct transfer from the SECD machine itself, influenced later languages including ML.

runtimes.name: SECD machine (conceptual)
runtimes.role: Landin's abstract stack-based machine (Stack, Environment, Control, Dump) used to give ISWIM-style expressions a precise operational semantics.
